To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) users can be provided with explanations in terms of their own vocabulary that are generated by a model trained to predict user behavior, 2) these explanations can be generated in an efficient manner by using a model of the task that is trained to predict human behavior and 3) users can be trained to provide more informative feedback that can improve the performance of the model over time.

(1) we can generate contrastive explanations for sequential decision-making tasks using a combination of symbolic planning, model learning and model-based planning, (2) users find these explanations useful, and (3) we find that the combination of model learning and model based planning can be used to improve performance of model-based planners on sequential decision-making problems.

(1) users are more satisfied with the explanations generated using our approach than with explanations generated using the current state-of-the-art methods and that (2) users are also able to identify the correct action for the task using the explanations provided by our approach.

the proposed methods are capable of generating contrastive explanations for a range of sequential decision-making problems, and that these explanations are perceived as helpful by users in the context of the tasks.
our methods are able to provide useful and understandable post-hoc explanations for the user, and that these methods can be extended to other domains and other AI systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to provide explanations for sequential decision-making problems that are not only understandable by the users but also allow them to challenge the AI's decision-making process.
even though the user-specified concepts may not be the best representation for the task, users can still find explanations in terms of these concepts useful.
